title: Gas kinematics of key prebiotic molecules in GV Tau N revealed with an ALMA, PdBI, and Herschel synergy
question: What are the physical structure, kinematics, and chemistry of the dense gas in the planet-forming region of GV Tau N, including the origin of water and organic molecules?

data.angular_resolution: 0.07" x 0.04" PA 27 deg (~12 au x 7 au) for HCN 3→2; 0.06" x 0.03" PA 27 deg for 1.1 mm continuum

what.value: Distance (d=180±17 pc) and proper motions (+8.695±0.853, -25.085±0.672 mas yr^-1) of GV Tau N

evidence.quote: GV Tau (Haro 6-10) is a T Tauri binary system embedded in the L1524 molecular cloud (d=180±17 pc) (Gaia Collaboration 2018).
The most recent estimation of the proper motions of GV Tau N are (+8.695±0.853) mas yr [−][1] in right ascension, and (−25.085± 0.672) mas yr [−][1] in declination (Gaia Collaboration 2018).

what.value: 3.6 cm continuum flux of 0.10±0.01 mJy towards GV Tau N

evidence.quote: Reipurth et al. (2004) measured a 3.6 cm flux of 0.10±0.01 mJy towards GV Tau N.

what.value: Previous PdBI 1.1 mm continuum position and HCN 3→2 total flux of 3.64±0.21 Jy km s^-1 in 0.32" x 0.25"

evidence.quote: This position is offset 0.19 [′′] to the South as compared to the position measured by Fuente et al. (2012)
Fuente et al. (2012) derived a total flux of 3.64±0.21 Jy×km s [−][1] in a region of 0.32 [′′] × 0.25 [′′] .

what.value: VLTI/MIDI mid-IR interferometric model temperatures, radii, and inclination i = 80 deg for GV Tau N disc

evidence.quote: Mid-infrared interferometry (VLTI/MIDI) observations to probe the circumstellar material around GV Tau N and S were carried out by Roccatagliata et al. (2011).
Based on the measureded visibilities, they estimate an inclination, i = 80 [◦] for the GV Tau N disc.

what.value: Position angles of Herbig-Haro flows: PA=222 deg (Jet 1) and PA=195 deg (Jet 2)

evidence.quote: the red lobe is close to the direction defined by the giant Herbig Haro flow, PA=222 [◦] (Devine et al. 1999) (hereafter, Jet 1), and the blue lobe is placed at PA=195 [◦], the direction of the Herbig Haro jet detected by Movsessian & Magakian (1999) (hereafter, Jet 2).

what.value: NIR molecular absorption rotation temperatures and column densities of 12CO, 13CO, C18O, C2H2, CH4, CO2, and HCN, plus stellar mass M~0.8 M_sun and absorption velocity v_lsr = 8.7±0.3 km s^-1

evidence.quote: Both stars have been classified as Class I objects with masses of M∼0.8 M ⊙ and ages of ∼ 3 Myr (Doppmann et al. 2008).
It is interesting to note that Doppmann et al. (2008) detected HCN and C 2 H 2 absorbing gas at v lsr = 8.7±0.3 km s [−][1]
References: (1) Gibb et al. 2007, 2008; (2) Doppmann et al. 2008; (3) Bast et al. 2013; (4) Gibb & Horne 2013

external_data.citation: Gibb et al. 2007, 2008; Doppmann et al. 2008; Bast et al. 2013; Gibb & Horne 2013

recipe.goal: Measure 1.1 mm continuum source properties and spectral index of the extended jet
recipe.method: Fit a 2D Gaussian to the compact 1.1 mm continuum source to derive flux, position, and size; measure flux of the extended jet component and compare with literature 3.6 cm flux to compute spectral index.
key_parameters: Position of continuum source adopted as offset (0",0") at alpha(J2000)=04h29m23.731s, delta(J2000)=24d33m01.11s

recipe.goal: Map HCN 3→2 morphology and kinematics and extract PdBI/ALMA spectra
recipe.method: Generate zero, first, and second moment maps (using channels >3sigma for moment 0), channel maps, and position-velocity diagrams along outflow axes (Jet 1 at PA=222 deg, Jet 2 at PA=195 deg) and perpendicular disc axes (D1, D2); overlay Keplerian velocity curves on D1 p-v diagram.
key_parameters: Jet 1 PA = 222 deg, Jet 2 PA = 195 deg, systemic velocity v_lsr = 6.3 km s^-1
assumptions: Stellar mass M_* = 0.8 M_sun and trial inclinations i = 20 deg, 40 deg, and 65 deg for Keplerian curves

recipe.goal: Decompose and fit Herschel/HIFI far-IR line profiles
recipe.method: Fit Gaussian components to Herschel/HIFI spectra of H2O, 13CO 10→9, HCN 7→6, and CN 5→4, decomposing water lines into a wide (FWHP ~ 8 km s^-1) and a narrow (FWHP ~ 2.7 km s^-1) component.

recipe.goal: Derive molecular column densities and abundance ratios across spatial scales
recipe.method: Analyze line intensity ratios and fit line profiles under Local Thermodynamic Equilibrium (LTE) for FIR (H2O, 13CO, HCN, CN) and mm interferometric (PdBI 13CO 3→2 and R<0.18" averaged ALMA HCN 3→2) transitions; compare with NIR absorption values.
key_parameters: Averaging radius R < 0.18" for ALMA HCN 3→2 to match PdBI 13CO 3→2 beam (~0.3")
assumptions: T_rot ~ 500 K and source size 0.5" for wide FIR H2O component; T_rot = 250 K and source size 18.5" for narrow FIR 13CO, HCN, and CN lines
T_rot = 250-500 K for mm interferometric 13CO 3→2 and HCN 3→2 emission

score_reason: The ALMA project code (2016.1.00813.S) and Herschel observation ID (OT1_afuente_2) are publicly available, and the analysis steps (2D Gaussian fit, moment maps, PV diagrams, Gaussian line fits, and LTE column density estimates) are straightforward. However, the ALMA data were manually calibrated and imaged without stating the weighting, robust parameter, self-calibration, or continuum subtraction details, and the PdBI dataset is not directly linked.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA Cycle 4 dataset (2016.1.00813.S) is public in the ALMA archive, and the core ALMA results—compact 1.1 mm continuum flux (~48 mJy) and size (94x66 mas), extended jet flux (4.6 mJy), HCN 3->2 ring radii (0.04"-0.18"), integrated flux (~1.4 Jy/beam km/s), and PV diagram kinematics—are concrete quantitative measurements that an agent can attempt to reproduce from the raw archival data.
